 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. Brentford are set to visit the Amex Stadium to take on Brighton and Hove Albion on Sunday. 
 The Bees are seventh in the table and head into the game five points behind the host in third place.
 They're also just two points outside the Champions League places, so beating the Seagulls away from home would help Brentford gatecrash the top four race.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Brentford have started the season in fine form, but Keith Andrews' men have struggled for consistency since the international break.
 They'd gone four games without a win (D2, L2) before returning to winning ways last weekend with a 2-0 win over Nottingham Forest at the Gtech Community Stadium.
 An own goal from Nikola Milenkovic gave the Bees the lead before Igor Thiago scored for the second consecutive match to secure all three points.
 Brentford will now aim to record consecutive Premier League wins for the first time since beating Aston Villa and Newcastle United in early February.
 However, they've failed to do so in nine consecutive Premier League games on the road, although they're unbeaten in four away matches this season (D4).
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement The Amex hasn't been a happy hunting ground for the Bees. They haven't won there since a 2-0 win in the Championship a decade ago.
 Caoimhin Kelleher starts in goal, with Michael Kayode, Kristoffer Ajer, Sepp van den Berg, and Keane Lewis-Potter lining up in defence.
 Vitaly Janelt and Mamadou Sangare did a decent job anchoring the midfield in the win over Forest, but the latter could be dropped for the Brighton clash.
 Sangare was widely tipped to be the Premier League signing of the season after joining Brentford earlier in the campaign but has struggled to reach those same heights since.
 With Yehor Yarmolyuk set to return after serving a three-match suspension, Sangare may have to make way to accommodate the Ukrainian midfielder, who has made 117 appearances for the Bees.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Jaidon Anthony could also come in for Dango Outtara after delivering an assist in an 18-minute cameo last time out, joining Mathias Jensen and Kevin Schade in attack.
 Brazilian striker Thiago will be keen to pick up where he left off after scoring in back-to-back games against Sunderland and Forest.
